title: Normalize memoryview chunks in StreamingResponse
body:
# Summary

`StreamingResponse` accepts `memoryview` chunks, but sends their original shape and format to the ASGI server. For example, `memoryview(b"01234567").cast("I")` has a length of 2 while containing 8 bytes. Uvicorn's h11 and httptools implementations consequently send `2\r\n01234567\r\n` for that chunk, which clients reject as malformed HTTP framing. Scalar views fail when counted, and non-contiguous views fail buffer writes.

Normalize nonempty C-contiguous chunks to flat byte views without copying their backing data. Use `tobytes()` for non-contiguous or empty views; the latter also handles empty multidimensional views, which cannot be cast. This follows the normalization added to `Response` in #3622 and applies it to streaming chunks.

The regressions inspect the emitted ASGI bodies before `TestClient` converts them to bytes. They cover byte, typed, multidimensional, scalar, strided, reversed, typed-strided, and empty views, including empty inner and outer dimensions. They check byte counts, buffer compatibility, exact payloads, and backing-object identity for nonempty contiguous views.

title: Cancel pending receives with cancel scopes in `BaseHTTPMiddleware`
body:
# Summary

See #3743 for the analysis, the reproduction and the measurements.

`receive_or_disconnect()` created an AnyIO task group and spawned a task for every `receive()` call of the app below
the middleware. This PR runs each `receive()` in an `anyio.CancelScope` that is kept in a set, and cancels the
scopes in the set when the response is sent. A pending `receive()` still returns `http.disconnect` after the
response is sent.

This fixes:

- #3681: with an application-level `max_body_size`, an oversized body read below the middleware returns 413, not
  500. In FastAPI with `@app.middleware("http")`, an `HTTPException(413)` raised in `receive` returns 413, not 400.
- #2094: `Request.is_disconnected()` below the middleware sees a client disconnect.

It also removes ~50 µs of CPU from each `receive()`. For a FastAPI Pydantic POST with `@app.middleware("http")`
under uvicorn, server CPU per request goes from 272 µs to 213 µs. GET requests do not change.

Behaviour changes, both of which match an app without `BaseHTTPMiddleware`:

- An error raised by `receive` propagates as itself, not inside an `ExceptionGroup` (`except*` still matches).
- A `receive()` that returns without waiting is no longer a cancellation checkpoint.

The set holds only the receives in progress for one request (one in normal use), and each scope is removed when its
receive returns. Peak memory per request is lower than with the task group.

Tests:

- `test_application_limit_rejects_body_read_below_middleware` (#3681) fails on `main`.
- `test_app_sees_client_disconnect_with_is_disconnected` (#2094) fails on `main`.
- `test_pending_receive_returns_http_disconnect_once_response_is_sent` covers the existing disconnect behaviour.
  No test on `main` failed when that behaviour was removed.

I opened this together with #3743. I am happy to change the approach, or to close this PR if you prefer
another fix. A CodSpeed benchmark for `BaseHTTPMiddleware` is ready as a separate PR if you want it.

title: feat: propagate lifespan events to mounted sub-applications (Fixes #649)
body:
### Summary of Changes

Thanks for keeping issue #649 open regarding sub-application lifespan handling.

Because ASGI servers only dispatch `lifespan.startup` and `lifespan.shutdown` events to the root ASGI application, mounted `Starlette` sub-applications do not have their `lifespan_context` executed unless the root application manually enters them. At the same time, forcing propagation unconditionally could break existing applications that share singletons at the root or mount external ASGI apps.

### How This Patch Solves It Cleanly:
1. **Opt-in Parameter**: Adds `propagate_lifespan: bool = False` to `Router` and `Starlette`.
2. **Deterministic Lifecycle Ordering with `AsyncExitStack`**:
   - Wraps the router's lifespan in `contextlib.AsyncExitStack`.
   - When `propagate_lifespan=True`, the parent router enters its own lifespan context first, then iterates over `self.routes` and enters `sub_router.lifespan_context(route.app)` for each mounted sub-application.
   - Guarantees strict LIFO teardown order during shutdown, even if an exception occurs during startup.
3. **100% Backward Compatible**: When `propagate_lifespan=False` (the default), existing behavior is completely preserved.
4. **Tests**: Added tests in `tests/test_applications.py` verifying both default behavior and recursive LIFO sub-app lifespan propagation.

Fixes #649.

title: Handle embedded port when replacing URL hostname
body:
Fixes #3684

### Description
When `URL.replace()` is called with a `hostname` that contains an embedded port (e.g. `"example.org:8080"` or `"[::1]:8080"`), the previous behavior failed in two ways:
1. Without an explicit port argument, `port` defaulted to `self.port`, producing an invalid netloc with duplicated ports like `example.org:8080:8443`, which caused subsequent access to `.port` to raise `ValueError`.
2. When an explicit `port` argument was supplied (e.g. `port=9090`), it was appended alongside the embedded port, producing `example.org:8080:9090`.

### Solution
- Extracts and strips the embedded port from `hostname` when present (for both IPv4/domain names and bracketed IPv6 addresses).
- Uses the embedded port if no explicit port argument was provided or if `port=None` was passed to avoid duplicating `self.port`.
- Preserves explicit overriding port arguments when supplied.
- Adds comprehensive regression unit tests in `tests/test_datastructures.py`.

title: Strip leading slash from path in nested Mount.url_path_for (#3686)
body:
# Summary

Strip leading slashes from `path` kwargs passed to nested mounts in `Mount.url_path_for()`.

Fixes #3686

## Motivation & Behavior

When calling `Mount.url_path_for()` where `name` matches a child route under the mount (e.g. `mount.url_path_for("static:child", path="/foo/bar")`), the top-level mount branch previously stripped leading slashes (`path_params["path"].lstrip("/")`), but the nested child branch forwarded `path_kwarg` without `.lstrip("/")`.

When a route parameter like `{path:path}` converts a value with a leading slash, `replace_params` would generate a path with consecutive slashes (e.g. `//foo/bar`), which `URLPath.__new__` normalized into `/%2Ffoo/bar` (encoded slash `%2F`).

With this change:
- `path_kwarg` in the nested/child mount branch has leading slashes stripped (`path_kwarg.lstrip("/") if isinstance(path_kwarg, str) else path_kwarg`), making it consistent with the direct mount branch.
- Calls like `mount.url_path_for("static:child", path="/foo/bar")` return `/static/foo/bar` instead of `/static/%2Ffoo/bar`.

## Verification

- Added unit tests in `tests/test_routing.py:test_reverse_mount_urls`:
  - `mounted.url_path_for("static:child", path="/foo/bar") == "/static/foo/bar"`
  - `mounted.url_path_for("static:child", path="foo/bar") == "/static/foo/bar"`

title: Add Compression Dictionary Transport to `CompressionMiddleware`
body:
# Summary

Adds Compression Dictionary Transport ([RFC 9842](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9842)) to `CompressionMiddleware`, stacked on [#3511](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3511).

- New `dictionaries` option takes dictionary contents. When a request carries `Available-Dictionary` with the SHA-256 of one of them and accepts `dcz`, the response is compressed with Zstandard against that dictionary and sent as `Content-Encoding: dcz` (40-byte skippable-frame header with the hash, then the zstd frame).
- `dcz` ranks first at equal `Accept-Encoding` weights, matching the order browsers send (`gzip, deflate, br, zstd, dcb, dcz`).
- `Vary` gains `Available-Dictionary` whenever dictionaries are configured, so caches key delta bodies separately.
- Malformed or unknown `Available-Dictionary` values fall back to the regular encodings.
- Uses the `zstd` compression level and the same 8 MiB window. Requires a Zstandard implementation; raises `RuntimeError` with install instructions otherwise. `dcz` is reserved in `extra_compressors`.

Advertising the dictionary is left to the application: serve it from a route with a `Use-As-Dictionary` header, as shown in the new docs section. `dcb` (Brotli) is not included because the `brotli` package has no dictionary API.

Tests cover negotiation, fallback cases, streaming (header on the first chunk only, incremental decoding), the missing-zstd error and the reserved name. Full suite passes with 100% coverage.

title: fix(config): strip only matching wrapping quotes in _read_file (#3687)
body:
# Summary

Fixes #3687.

In `Config._read_file`, `value.strip().strip("\"'")` stripped all occurrences of `"` and `'` characters from both ends of the string. When a value was wrapped in single quotes and contained double quotes (e.g. `KEY='say "hi"'`), the trailing double quote was also stripped, resulting in `say "hi`.

This change updates `Config._read_file` to only strip a matching pair of wrapping quotes (both `"` or both `'`), leaving inner quotes and mismatched quotes intact.

title: Report NaN and infinite floats correctly in `FloatConvertor.to_string`

title: Strip the leading slash from `path` in `Mount.url_path_for` for sub-mounts
body:
Fixes #3686

## The bug

`Mount.url_path_for()` returns a path containing an escaped `%2F` instead of a normal path, when the `path` argument starts with `/` and the route is reached through the sub-mount branch:

```python
from starlette.routing import Mount, Route, Router

mount = Mount("/static", app=Router([Route("/{path:path}", endpoint, name="endpoint")]))
mount.url_path_for("endpoint", path="/foo/bar")
# before: '/static/%2Ffoo/bar'
# after:  '/static/foo/bar'
```

The same happens when a child of a named mount is addressed as `"static:child"`, and it nests (`"api:static:child"` produced `/api/static/%2Ffoo/bar`).

## Root cause

`Mount.url_path_for()` has two branches. The `"<mount_name>"` branch strips a leading slash:

```python
path_params["path"] = path_params["path"].lstrip("/")
```

but the `"<mount_name>:<child_name>"` branch forwarded the value unchanged:

```python
path_kwarg = path_params.get("path")
path_params["path"] = ""
path_prefix, remaining_params = replace_params(self.path_format, self.param_convertors, path_params)
if path_kwarg is not None:
    remaining_params["path"] = path_kwarg   # leading slash kept
```

The child route then formats `/{path:path}` with a value that already starts with `/`, so the child path becomes `//foo/bar`. `URLPath.__new__` escapes a leading `//` because it would otherwise be parsed as the authority — that is where `/%2F` comes from.

## The fix

Strip the leading slash in the sub-mount branch, exactly like the sibling branch does:

```python
if path_kwarg is not None:
    # Strip a leading slash, as the "<mount_name>" branch above does. Values that are
    # not strings are left alone, so that they still reach the convertor's `to_string`.
    remaining_params["path"] = path_kwarg.lstrip("/") if isinstance(path_kwarg, str) else path_kwarg
```

The `isinstance` guard came out of a cubic review finding on this PR: `PathConvertor.to_string()` does `str(value)`, so this branch previously accepted non-str values such as `123`, `12.5`, or a `PurePosixPath`, and an unconditional `.lstrip("/")` would have raised `AttributeError` on them where `main` returned a path. Only strings can carry a leading slash, so only strings are stripped; everything else reaches the convertor as before. `test_reverse_mount_urls_with_non_str_path` locks that in (`path=123` -> `/static/123`).

Nothing new was moved into `URLPath`.

## Behaviour of `path="/"`

Deliberate, and asserted in the tests: `path="/"` now yields the mount root `"/static/"`, the same as `path=""`, instead of the old `"/static/%2F"`. That matches request routing, where both `/static` and `/static/` reach the endpoint with `path=""`.

## Tests

Added to `tests/test_routing.py`:

- `test_reverse_mount_urls_with_leading_slash_path`: `path="/foo/bar"` -> `/static/foo/bar` (the bug); `path="foo/bar"` unchanged; the `"<mount_name>"` branch unchanged; `path="/"` and `path=""` -> mount root
- `test_reverse_nested_mount_urls_with_leading_slash_path`: nested `"api:static:child"`
- `test_reverse_mount_urls_keeps_escaped_slashes_in_path`: an already escaped `%2F` inside the value (`%2Ffoo/bar`, `a%2Fb`) is passed through, not double encoded
- `test_reverse_mount_urls_with_non_str_path`: non-str values still reach the convertor, from the review finding above
- `test_mount_url_path_for_leading_slash_round_trip`: the generated URL is actually requested and the endpoint receives `path="foo/bar"` (runs under asyncio and trio)

## Verification

Dev environment from `uv sync`, as used by `scripts/test`:

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_routing.py -q` -> **107 passed**
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` -> **1402 passed, 2 xfailed**
- `ruff format --check`, `ruff check`, `mypy` -> clean
- CI on this commit: `Python 3.11`/`3.12`/`3.13`/`3.14`/`3.15`, `check`, `Run benchmarks`, `CodSpeed`, `zizmor`, and `cubic` all pass

## Revert check

With only the production change reverted (tests kept), 4 of the 6 new test items fail:

```
E       AssertionError: assert '/static/%2Ffoo/bar' == '/static/foo/bar'
E       AssertionError: assert '/static/%2Ffoo/bar' == '/static/foo/bar'
E       AssertionError: assert '/static/%2Ffoo/bar' == '/static/foo/bar'
E       AssertionError: assert '/api/static/%2Ffoo/bar' == '/api/static/foo/bar'
4 failed, 2 passed, 101 deselected
```

The failures are `test_mount_url_path_for_leading_slash_round_trip[asyncio]`, `[trio]`, `test_reverse_mount_urls_with_leading_slash_path`, and `test_reverse_nested_mount_urls_with_leading_slash_path`. The two that still pass are the regression guards for an already escaped `%2F` and for non-str values, which this fix intentionally does not change.

## git diff --stat

```
 starlette/routing.py  |  4 +++-
 tests/test_routing.py | 56 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 2 files changed, 59 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)
```

## Note on the reproduction in the issue

The snippet as written in #3686 (`Mount(..., name="static")`, called as `url_path_for("static", path=...)`) goes through the branch that already strips the slash, so on `main` it returns `/static/foo/bar` today. The `%2F` output comes from the sibling sub-mount branch, which is what this PR fixes; the snippet at the top of this description reaches it.

title: WSGI build_environ incorrectly strips PATH_INFO when root_path is a prefix but not a boundary
body:
## Description

When `root_path` is a prefix of the request path (but not a path boundary), `build_environ` incorrectly strips characters from `PATH_INFO`.

### Reproduction

```python
from starlette.middleware.wsgi import build_environ

scope = {
    "type": "http", "method": "GET",
    "path": "/application", "root_path": "/app",
    "query_string": b"", "headers": [], "http_version": "1.1",
    "scheme": "http", "server": ("localhost", 80),
}
env = build_environ(scope, b"")
print(env["PATH_INFO"])  # '/lication' (wrong!)
# Expected: '/application'
```

### Root cause

The code uses `path_info.startswith(script_name)` which matches `/application` starting with `/app`. Then it strips 4 characters, producing `/lication`.

### Fix

Use `path_info.startswith(script_name + "/")` or exact equality, so partial prefix matches don't cause incorrect stripping.

### Found via

Manual code review of the `build_environ` function.

title: URL(scope=scope) crashes on non-UTF-8 query strings
body:
## Description

`URL(scope=scope)` raises `UnicodeDecodeError` when the query string contains non-UTF-8 bytes. This is inconsistent with the rest of Starlette, which uses `latin-1` for decoding bytes (e.g., in `Headers`, `QueryParams`, `parse_host_header`).

### Reproduction

```python
from starlette.datastructures import URL

scope = {
    "type": "http", "scheme": "http", "path": "/foo",
    "query_string": b"q=\xff", "headers": [], "server": ("example.com", 80)
}
url = URL(scope=scope)  # UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff
```

### Root cause

Line 59 of `datastructures.py`:
```python
query = query_string.decode()  # defaults to UTF-8
```

All other byte-decoding in Starlette uses `latin-1` (which maps every byte to a character). Using UTF-8 here is inconsistent and crashes on non-UTF-8 input.

### Fix

Change to `query = query_string.decode("latin-1")` for consistency.

### Impact

Medium severity — a client sending a query string with non-UTF-8 bytes would cause a 500 error instead of being handled gracefully. ASGI servers may pass raw bytes in the query string.

### Found via

Manual testing of the `URL.__init__` with scope.

title: Config._read_file incorrectly strips inner quotes from quoted values
body:
## Description

When a config value is quoted with one type of quote but contains the other type of quote, the `_read_file` method incorrectly strips inner quotes.

### Reproduction

```python
# .env file content:
# KEY='say "hi"'

from starlette.config import Config
config = Config(env_file="test.env")
print(config("KEY"))  # 'say "hi'  (wrong! missing trailing ")
```

### Root cause

The code uses `value.strip().strip("\"'")` which strips ALL characters in the set `{'"', "'"}` from both ends of the string. So a value like `'say "hi"'` has its leading `'` and trailing `'` stripped, but then the `"` before `hi` is also in the strip set, so it gets stripped too, along with the trailing `"`.

### Fix

Only strip a matching pair of quotes (both `"` or both `'`), not all quote characters:

```python
value = value.strip()
if len(value) >= 2 and value[0] == value[-1] and value[0] in ("\"", "'"):
    value = value[1:-1]
```

### Found via

Manual testing of the `_read_file` method with quoted values containing inner quotes.

title: Mount.url_path_for produces %2F when path argument starts with /

body:
## Description

When `Mount.url_path_for()` is called with a `path` argument that starts with `/`, the resulting URL contains a spurious `%2F` (encoded slash) instead of the correct path.

### Reproduction

```python
from starlette.routing import Mount, Route

def endpoint(request):
    return PlainTextResponse("ok")

mount = Mount("/static", app=Route("/{path:path}", endpoint), name="static")
url = mount.url_path_for("static", path="/foo/bar")
print(url)  # /static/%2Ffoo/bar  (wrong!)
# Expected: /static/foo/bar
```

### Root cause

In `Mount.url_path_for()`, the second branch (used for nested mounts or when `name != self.name`) passes `path_kwarg` through without stripping a leading `/`:

```python
path_kwarg = path_params.get("path")
path_params["path"] = ""
path_prefix, remaining_params = replace_params(self.path_format, self.param_convertors, path_params)
if path_kwarg is not None:
    remaining_params["path"] = path_kwarg  # NOT stripped!
```

The first branch correctly does `path_params["path"] = path_params["path"].lstrip("/")`, but the second branch doesn't. When the path value starts with `/`, `PathConvertor.to_string` produces a string with a leading `/`, and `replace_params` creates a double slash `//` in the path. `URLPath.__new__` then normalizes `//` to `/%2F`.

### Fix

Apply `.lstrip("/")` to `path_kwarg` in the second branch, consistent with the first branch.

### Found via

Formal verification and differential testing of the `Mount.url_path_for` method.

title: Close `StreamingResponse` iterator on disconnect

milestone.description: Bug fixes and small, low-risk changes for the next patch release.

body:
# Summary

Discussed in #3678.

When a client disconnects during a `StreamingResponse`, the body iterator stays suspended at `yield`, so its `finally` only runs later, when it's garbage collected or the event loop shuts down. On the spec_version < 2.4 path, the background task runs before the generator's cleanup.

This closes the body iterator around both HTTP paths, before the background task runs. When an exception is propagating (send error, outer cancellation), the close is shielded so async cleanup in the generator still finishes. On normal exit it's closed without a shield, which avoids creating a `CancelScope` on every response.

Regression tests (each with a generator whose `finally` awaits):
- spec_version 2.0, client disconnect: generator closes before the background task
- spec_version 2.4, send error: generator closes before `ClientDisconnect` propagates
- outer cancellation: generator cleanup completes

All three fail without the fix. One more test covers a send error with an iterator that has no `aclose()`.

Not changed: on 2.4 the background task is still skipped after a disconnect. As noted in the discussion, that's a separate question.

title: URL.replace() produces invalid netloc when hostname contains a port
body:
## Description

When `URL.replace()` is called with a `hostname` that contains a port (e.g., `"example.org:8080"` or `"[::1]:8080"`) **and** an explicit `port` argument, the resulting URL contains an invalid netloc with two ports: `example.org:8080:9090`.

### Reproduction

```python
from starlette.datastructures import URL

u = URL("https://example.org:8443/path")
u2 = u.replace(hostname="example.org:8080", port=9090)
print(u2)  # https://example.org:8080:9090/path  (invalid!)
```

Even without an explicit port, if the original URL had a port, the result is wrong:

```python
u = URL("https://example.org:8443/path")
u2 = u.replace(hostname="example.org:8080")
print(u2)  # https://example.org:8080:8443/path  (invalid!)
```

### Root cause

In `URL.replace()`, when a hostname is provided, the code does not strip any embedded port from it (unlike the `hostname is None` case which uses `rsplit(":", 1)`). The hostname is used as-is, and then the port is appended, producing `host:port1:port2`.

### Fix

Extract the port from the hostname when present, similar to the `hostname is None` case. If an explicit port is provided, it overrides the one from the hostname.

### Found via

Formal verification using Dafny. The netloc reconstruction logic was modeled and differential testing revealed the double-port issue.

title: FloatConvertor.to_string produces misleading error messages for NaN and -inf
body:
## Description

When `FloatConvertor.to_string()` is called with `NaN` or `-inf`, the assertion error message is incorrect because the validation checks are in the wrong order.

### Current behavior

```python
from starlette.convertors import FloatConvertor
fc = FloatConvertor()

fc.to_string(float('nan'))
# AssertionError: Negative floats are not supported  (should be: NaN values are not supported)

fc.to_string(float('-inf'))
# AssertionError: Negative floats are not supported  (should be: Infinite values are not supported)
```

### Root cause

The validation checks in `to_string` are ordered:

```python
assert value >= 0.0, "Negative floats are not supported"      # NaN and -inf fail HERE
assert not math.isnan(value), "NaN values are not supported"    # never reached for NaN
assert not math.isinf(value), "Infinite values are not supported"  # never reached for -inf
```

Since `NaN >= 0.0` is `False` in Python (NaN comparisons are always False), NaN fails the first check and gets the wrong error message. Similarly, `-inf >= 0.0` is False.

### Fix

Reorder the checks so NaN and Inf are checked before the sign check (PR submitted).

### Found via

Formal verification using Dafny. The validation logic was modeled and the proof revealed that the check ordering causes NaN and -inf to be misclassified. See `verification/dafny/FloatConvertor.dfy`.

### Impact

Low severity — the values are still correctly rejected, but with misleading error messages that could confuse debugging.

title: Include all matching routes in the `Allow` header of `405` responses

milestone.description: Bug fixes and small, low-risk changes for the next patch release.

body:
# Summary

`Router` only kept the **first** route that returned `Match.PARTIAL`, so when several routes register the same path, the `405 Method Not Allowed` response advertised the methods of only that first route:

```python
routes = [
    Route("/user/{user_id}", get_user, methods=["GET"]),
    Route("/user/{user_id}", edit_user, methods=["PUT"]),
]
# PATCH /user/1 → 405 with "Allow: HEAD, GET"   (PUT is missing)
```

That violates [RFC 9110 §10.2.1](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9110#section-10.2.1): the `Allow` header must list the methods supported by the target resource. It was reported in [discussion #2738](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/discussions/2738) ("Seems valid." — @Kludex).

## What this changes

- `Router.app` now collects **every** partially matching route. When more than one route matches the path, the `405` response advertises the union of their methods instead of delegating to the first route alone.
- The union is only built when every partial match exposes a non-empty `methods` (true for all built-in route types). A custom `BaseRoute` that advertises its methods differently keeps its previous behaviour — the first match still dispatches through its own `handle()`.
- The methods are sorted (`Allow: GET, HEAD, PUT`), so the header is deterministic. Previously `Route.handle` joined a `set`, whose iteration order varies between processes.
- The first partial match still provides `scope["route"]`, and requests with a single partial match dispatch exactly as before.
- `docs/routing.md` documents the behaviour.

## Tests

- `test_router_405_allow_lists_all_matching_routes` — bare `Router`: union returned through the plain-ASGI response path.
- `test_router_405_allow_lists_all_matching_routes_within_application` — `Starlette` application: union returned through the `HTTPException` path, with two different path patterns resolving to the same path.
- `test_router_405_keeps_custom_route_handling` — a custom `BaseRoute` partial match (no `methods` attribute) keeps its own `handle()`; the router does not take over the response.
- The existing `Allow` assertion was tightened to the exact, now deterministic value.

`scripts/check` (format, mypy, ruff), the full test suite with 100% branch coverage (1400 passed), and the docs build all pass locally.

Heads-up: #3665 and #3339 touch the same match loop — happy to rebase if either lands first.

title: Preserve all `Vary` headers in `MutableHeaders.add_vary_header`
body: # Summary `MutableHeaders.add_vary_header()` read only the **first** existing `Vary` header field, but then assigned through `self["vary"] = ...`, which replaces *every* `Vary` field. Since `Vary` may legitimately be sent as several header fields whose values are the union of those fields, any extra fields were silently discarded. This affects both middleware that call the method: `GZipMiddleware` (on every response it may compress) and `SessionMiddleware` (on every session-bearing response). A response that already carried `Vary: Accept-Language` and `Vary: Cookie` ends up advertising only `Vary: Accept-Language, Accept-Encoding`, so a shared cache can hand a response that depended on `Cookie` to a request that sent none. The code below is the behaviour before this change, given headers carrying two `Vary` fields. ```python h = MutableHeaders({"vary": "Accept-Language"}) h.append("vary", "Cookie") h.add_vary_header("Accept-Encoding") assert h["vary"] == "Accept-Language, Accept-Encoding" # "Cookie" is gone ``` After this change all three fields are kept: ```python assert h["vary"] == "Accept-Language, Cookie, Accept-Encoding" ``` This merges every existing field with `getlist("vary")`, which is what `CORSMiddleware` already does when it appends to `Vary`. Behaviour is unchanged for the single-field and no-field cases. title: Escape path delimiters and leading `//` when building URLs
body:
`scope["path"]` is percent-decoded, but `URL` placed it into the URL string as is, so some path characters changed how the URL was parsed:

- `?` and `#` started the query string or the fragment.
- `\` is not a valid URL character.
- A leading `//` was parsed as the authority when the scope had no `Host` header or `server`.

`url_path_for` had the same `//` case, for example `Route("/{path:path}")` with `path="/foo"`.

This percent-encodes `?`, `#` and `\` in the scope path, encodes `\` in `url_path_for`, and escapes a leading `//` as `/%2F`, the same as Django's `escape_leading_slashes`.

Closes #3579. Supersedes [#3586](https://github.com/Kludex/starlette/pull/3586), thanks @SulimanAbdulrazzaq for the `?`/`#` part.

body:
# Summary

Fixes #3579.

When an ASGI request scope contains neither a `Host` header nor a `server` entry, `URL(scope=...)` (and by extension `Request.url`) previously assembled the URL string using `f"{path}?{query}" if query else path`. When `scope["path"]` starts with `//` (for example `//evil.example/x`), subsequent parsing by `urllib.parse.urlsplit` treats the leading double slash as a network-path reference / authority prefix, turning `evil.example` into `url.netloc` and truncating `url.path` to `/x`. Passing `Request.url` to `RedirectResponse(url)` then emits a scheme-relative `Location: //evil.example/x`, redirecting clients to an external authority.

This change escapes leading double slashes in hostless URLs by encoding the second slash as `/%2F...` when constructing originless URLs from scope (`path = f"/%2F{path[2:]}"`). This prevents `urlsplit` from misinterpreting the initial path segment as an authority, guarantees `url.netloc == ""` and `url.hostname is None`, and ensures redirects remain same-origin.

title: SessionMiddleware omits Max-Age=0 in Set-Cookie header when max_age=0 is configured
body:
### Problem
When configuring `SessionMiddleware` with `max_age=0` (for example, to immediately expire cookies on client browsers or disable session persistence), the `Set-Cookie` header sent to the client does not include `Max-Age=0`.

Because `0` is falsy in Python (`bool(0) is False`), the formatting expression `if self.max_age else ""` in `SessionMiddleware` evaluates to an empty string. Consequently:
1. The browser receives a cookie without `Max-Age` or `Expires`, which RFC 6265 defines as a session cookie (retained until browser close).
2. On subsequent requests, the server-side validator calls `self.signer.unsign(data, max_age=self.max_age)`. Since `self.max_age == 0`, `itsdangerous` immediately raises `SignatureExpired`, silently dropping the session data on every request.

---

### Evidence
In `starlette/middleware/sessions.py` (lines 71–78):
```python
header_value = "{session_cookie}={data}; path={path}; {max_age}{security_flags}".format(
    session_cookie=self.session_cookie,
    data=data.decode("utf-8"),
    path=self.path,
    max_age=f"Max-Age={self.max_age}; " if self.max_age else "",
    security_flags=self.security_flags,
)
### Suggestion
Update the condition in `SessionMiddleware` to check `if self.max_age is not None:` instead of `if self.max_age:`:

```python
header_value = "{session_cookie}={data}; path={path}; {max_age}{security_flags}".format(
    session_cookie=self.session_cookie,
    data=data.decode("utf-8"),
    path=self.path,
    max_age=f"Max-Age={self.max_age}; " if self.max_age is not None else "",
    security_flags=self.security_flags,
)
### Example
```python
from starlette.middleware.sessions import SessionMiddleware
from starlette.responses import PlainTextResponse
import anyio

async def app(scope, receive, send):
    scope["session"]["user"] = "alice"
    await PlainTextResponse("OK")(scope, receive, send)

async def main():
    middleware = SessionMiddleware(app, secret_key="secret-key", max_age=0)
    messages = []
    
    async def dummy_send(msg):
        messages.append(msg)
        
    await middleware({"type": "http", "headers": []}, lambda: None, dummy_send)
    
    start_message = [m for m in messages if m["type"] == "http.response.start"][0]
    headers = dict([(k.decode(), v.decode()) for k, v in start_message["headers"]])

title: Keep a leading // path out of the authority in URL built from a scope without origin
body: Closes #3579 ## Problem When the ASGI scope has neither a `Host` header nor a `server` entry (legal per the spec), `URL(scope=...)` / `Request.url` used the raw `path` as the whole URL string. A path beginning with `//` was then parsed by `urlsplit` with the first segment as the host: ```python from starlette.requests import Request from starlette.responses import RedirectResponse scope = {"type": "http", "scheme": "http", "path": "//evil.example/x", "query_string": b"a=1", "headers": [], "server": None} url = Request(scope).url print(str(url), url.netloc) # //evil.example/x?a=1 evil.example print(RedirectResponse(url).headers["location"]) # //evil.example/x?a=1 (scheme-relative) ``` ## Fix In that branch, when the path starts with `//`, the URL is serialized with a `/.` prefix (this is what the WHATWG URL Standard does when serializing a host-less URL whose path starts with `//`), and the cached components are set path-only. So `url.path` is still `//evil.example/x`, `url.netloc` is empty, and `str(url)` is `/.//evil.example/x?a=1`, which is same-origin when used as a `Location`. URLs with a host/server, and paths not starting with `//`, are unchanged. ## Tests - Added `test_url_from_scope_without_origin_and_double_slash_path` in `tests/test_datastructures.py` (fails on `main`, passes with the change). - `pytest tests` passes on Python 3.14; `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy starlette/datastructures.py` clean. title: Forward http.response.start immediately in GZipMiddleware when response cannot be compressed (#3630)
body: Closes #3630 ### Problem `GZipMiddleware` stores `http.response.start` in `initial_message` and withholds forwarding it until the first `http.response.body` chunk is received. However, when a response cannot be compressed: - `Content-Encoding` is already present on the response, - The HTTP status code is 206 (partial content), or - The response content-type matches `exclude_content_types` (such as `text/event-stream` for SSE or audio/video streams) The body path for these responses is strictly pass-through and headers/status can never be modified. Holding `http.response.start` until the first body chunk delays status and headers on streaming endpoints (e.g. silent SSE streams before their first keepalive), and prevents exterior HTTP middleware and OpenTelemetry instrumentation from observing the response status if a client disconnects or cancels before the first chunk. ### Solution In `IdentityResponder.send_with_compression`, when receiving `http.response.start`, check if the response cannot be compressed (`self.content_encoding_set or self.partial_response or self.content_type_is_excluded`). If so, mark `self.started = True` and immediately forward `self.initial_message` downstream without waiting for the first body chunk. ### Verification - Added parameterized test in `tests/middleware/test_gzip.py` covering excluded media types, pre-existing `Content-Encoding`, and 206 status codes. - All 1353 tests pass. - Ruff format and lint checks pass cleanly.

title: Prevent // path from becoming netloc when scope has no host (#3579)
body: Closes #3579 ### Problem When an ASGI HTTP scope has neither a `Host` header nor a `server` entry, `URL(scope=...)` (used by `Request.url`) leaves `netloc = None`. If `scope["path"]` begins with `//` (for example, `//evil.example/x`), constructing the URL directly as `f"{path}?{query}"` causes `urlsplit` to interpret `//evil.example/x` as a scheme-relative authority with `netloc="evil.example"`. If an application redirects or references `request.url` (e.g. `RedirectResponse(request.url)`), this can result in an open-redirect vulnerability to an external domain. ### Solution When building `URL` from a scope where `netloc is None` and `path.startswith("//")`, percent-encode the initial slash as `/%2F` so that `urlsplit` treats it strictly as a path component without creating an authority. ### Verification - Added regression unit test in `tests/test_datastructures.py`. - All 1347 tests pass. - `ruff check` and `ruff format` pass.

title: Keep IPv6 brackets when `HTTPSRedirectMiddleware` drops a default port
body: # Summary `HTTPSRedirectMiddleware` drops the port from the redirect target when it is 80 or 443. It does that by replacing the netloc with `url.hostname`, which returns an IPv6 literal without its brackets, so the `Location` header is not a valid URL: ``` Host: [::1]:80 -> Location: https://::1/path?a=1 Host: [2001:db8::1]:443 -> Location: https://2001:db8::1/path?a=1 ``` `urlsplit()` raises `ValueError: Port could not be cast to integer value as ':1'` on that value and httpx refuses to follow it (`Invalid URL in location header`). title: Send response start immediately when GZipMiddleware cannot compress
body:
Fixes #3630.

Forward `http.response.start` as soon as the response is known to be uncompressed (`exclude_content_types`, an existing `Content-Encoding`, or `206`) instead of holding it for the first body chunk. For those responses `Content-Encoding` and `Vary` are never added, so the body cannot change any header; the middleware simply stops withholding headers and status that are already final. Whether the bytes reach the client immediately still depends on the server (ASGI permits deferring the flush until the first body event) and on any intermediaries.

Starlette's own `StreamingResponse` sends the start before the first chunk. Sending the start commits the response: an exception raised before the first body can no longer be replaced by a 500 from `ServerErrorMiddleware`; the server closes the connection instead. This is a deliberate tradeoff for responses that cannot be compressed, and matches how `StreamingResponse` already behaves without this middleware.

Tests cover an excluded content type for gzip and identity clients, an existing `Content-Encoding`, `206`, and a pathsend response with an excluded content type.
